title: Finite etale origins under completed-coefficient open extension
statement: Let j:U→T be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], let d be an adic coefficient datum on A with ideal I [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let K∈D(Mod(A_U)). If each positive quotient reduction K⊗ᴸ_(A_U)(A/I^(n+1))_U has a specified bounded-below etale origin [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], then each quotient reduction of j_!K, for the actual completed-coefficient extension [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], has a bounded-below etale origin on T. No completeness, quasi-compactness, common lower bound or compatibility of the supplied origins is assumed.

source.place: First paragraph: the reductions of j_!K are j_!K_n and carry the witnesses j_!L_n.

proof.text: Fix a positive quotient B=A/I^(n+1). The coefficient-linear finite comparison of lem-cbc-ringed-open-strict-reduction, computed on a flat-term K-flat representative, identifies reduction of completed-coefficient open extension with open extension of the B-reduction. Its formula is [x] tensor b maps to [x tensor b restricted to the open]; it is B-linear before scalar restriction. Descend from K-flat representatives.

Transport the finite function-coefficient ring to the constant coefficient ring using finiteOriginConstantIso. The same extension-summand formula intertwines this scalar restriction with exact open extension on constant B-module sheaves. Extend each retained bounded-below etale antecedent by etale open extension. The etale/pro-etale open comparison identifies its realization with extension of the original realization. Compose that comparison, extension of the supplied witness isomorphism, and the inverse finite reduction comparison of step 1.

Exact etale open extension preserves the lower cohomological bound of that particular antecedent. The preceding isomorphism therefore gives a FiniteEtaleOriginWitness for this quotient. Repeat independently for each n; no common lower bound or transition compatibility is used. For an empty open or a zero quotient ring the constructions are the zero functors, with the same unit and tensor formulas.

lean.statement:
theorem cbcCompletedOpenFiniteEtaleOrigins
    {A : Type (t + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    {U T : Scheme.{t}} (j : U ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (K : d.derived U)
    (W : ∀ n : ℕ, FiniteEtaleOriginWitness U (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))
      ((d.reduction U n).obj K)) :
    Nonempty (∀ n : ℕ, FiniteEtaleOriginWitness T (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))
      ((d.reduction T n).obj ((cbcDerivedOpenShriek d j inferInstance).obj K)))
